summary.title: Microsoft Security Development Lifecycle Practices
summary.one_liner: You learn the 10 key Microsoft SDL security practices and how they map to the design, code, build and deploy, run, and Zero Trust stages of development.
keywords: how to integrate security into development lifecycle
takeaways: The Microsoft SDL defines 10 key security practices meant to be integrated into every stage of development.
Security risks are considered in five areas: Design, Code, Build and Deploy, Run, and Zero Trust architecture and governance.
Design should avoid letting attackers easily reach the workload, its data, or business assets.
CI/CD pipelines should prevent unauthorized users from altering code, and the runtime environment should follow security baselines.
All stages should follow Zero Trust: assume breach, verify explicitly, and grant least privilege.
summary.summary: This Microsoft page introduces the Security Development Lifecycle (SDL) as a set of 10 key security practices to integrate security across the software development process. It organizes security risks by stage: Design, Code, Build and Deploy (CI/CD), Run (cloud, servers, devices), and an overarching Zero Trust architecture and governance layer. The excerpt describes goals for each stage but does not list the 10 practices themselves, and the page notes they will be updated over time.
